jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Are you a person who enjoys helping others? Are you currently seeking fulfillment in your professional life?

  

Hope Services is Silicon Valley’s leading provider of services to people with developmental disabilities and mental health needs. We seek candidates who share our inspirations & aspirations. Selection of staff is made on a competitive basis, and we are committed to promoting diversity, equity, inclusion & belonging at all levels..

**>>>>> 2025 Winner of Mercury News Best in Silicon Valley** **<<<<<**

**>>>>> ASPIRE to Excellence CARF Accredited** **<<<<<**

**>>>>> 2024 Great Nonprofits Top-Rated Nonprofit** **<<<<<**

**>>>>> Four-star Charity Navigator** **<<<<<**

**>>>>> 2024 Candid Gold Seal of Transparency** **<<<<<**

* **Compensation****: $5,859.00 per month**

**Purpose:**

Provides resources support and training to staff and clients to facilitate agency, program, and consumer goals. Supervision, hiring and training staff, budgeting and contract fulfillment, and assignments to perform or discharge special projects in areas of responsibility. Ensures maintenance of equipment, ordering of supplies, inventory and quality of service.

**Principle Responsibilities:**

The following responsibilities represent the essential functions of the position. An employee in this classification is responsible for carrying out the following functions:

1. Assures adequate program staffing through scheduling, recruitment, hiring,

and orientation of direct service, substitute and volunteer staff as assigned.

Provides all aspects of supervision, evaluation, and training of staff.

2. Acts as a resource for rehabilitation, program development, community

based employment and activities, acts as a liaison between program

services and the community.

3. Provides oversight of daily operations and services including case

management, communications, and advocacy, assures quality services are

provided in timely manner.

4. Assures timely communications with persons served, families, care

providers, funding sources, staff, management and community.

5. Participates in the development and implementation of the Agency planning

effort including departmental budgeting, policies and procedures, and the

implementation of Agency goals.

6. Oversees accuracy and timeliness of billing, payroll, funding, DOL

compliance, inventories, training records, and various internal and external

reports.

7. Conducts tours, presentations and client intakes.

8. Assures compliance with all safety regulations.

9. In the absence of a manager, if assigned, may act in that capacity.

10. Provides direct service in program operations as needed to assure adequate

staffing ratios.

11. Acts as a mandated abuse reporter.

12. May perform special projects or other duties as assigned to assure the

efficiency of the program.

**Minimum Qualifications**:

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent plus three years of related experience working with people with disabilities in a rehabilitation environment.

**Reports To:** Manager

**Supervisory Responsibility****:** yes

**Required knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

1. Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, database and spreadsheet

2. Ability to communicate effectively and provide excellent customer service

3. Ability to facilitate systems and checks to assure delivery of quality service

and product to internal and external customers

4. Knowledge of the principles of management, supervision, planning, fiscal

management, fair employment practices, regulations, safety, health and

client rights

5. Ability to observe, evaluate, document and communicate verbally and in

writing

6. Knowledge of rehabilitation and program development

**Environmental Conditions:**

Constant movement around service area, and travel into the community. Time spent sitting, using a computer station, periods of intense concentration, using the telephone, paperwork. Time spent in meetings, travel to various work site locations throughout three counties. Exposure to outdoor weather and environmental conditions.

Positions connected to a production environment are also exposed to times of fast paced activity, loud noise and to dust and airborne particles.

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Visit www.hopeservices.org to find out more about us and the people we serve.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator - HUB
jobs.description:
**About Bill Wilson Center:**  
Bill Wilson Center provides services to children, youth, young adults, and families in Santa Clara County. Additionally, we reach clients through our street outreach and crisis line programs. Bill Wilson Center programs focus on housing, mental health care, supportive services, and advocacy. Bill Wilson Center is committed to working with the community to ensure that every youth has access to the range of services needed to grow to be healthy and self-sufficient adults. A key component of Bill Wilson Center's philosophy encompasses a strength-based approach to improving the lives of the youth and young families in our communities. Bill Wilson Center has been providing services to runaway and homeless youth since 1973. Join us and become a difference maker at Bill Wilson Center!

**Job Summary:**  
In partnership with County of Santa Clara, Bill Wilson Center provides independent living skills and basic needs for foster youth. The HUB Coordinator welcomes and greets youth and provides orientation of facilities and services. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform all essential duties and responsibilities satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Essential Duties/Responsibilities:**

* Coordinate with the Hub/ILP Program Manager (PM) to ensure the opening and closing of the HUB and appropriate in-person coverage at the front desk. Provide copies of sign in sheets to the PM as requested.
* Assist staff to verify client eligibility.
* Ensure that client and program records are maintained and up to date, ensure data entry is timely in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) database as required.
* Provide reports as required to track client participation in services.
* Plan, coordinate and facilitate meetings, workshops and events. Create flyers and outreach messaging as necessary.
* Coordinate the daily monitoring and maintenance of basic services such as kitchen, showers, washers/dryers, and HUB Mart.
* Provide orientation and tours to clients, visitors and other stakeholders.
* Provide peer support to HUB members. Responsible for supervising clients on the HUB floor and ensuring rules and policies are being observed. Issue consequences to clients for violations and report incidents to the program manager immediately. Work cooperatively with all co-located partners to ensure safety of the HUB and adherence to all procedures.
* Mediate client concerns and conflict following applicable policies and procedures.
* Participate in outreach by text, phone, email and/or social media to engage them in services.
* Participate in administering and maintaining HUB Instagram, web site, and other social media accounts as directed.
* Responsible for soliciting food and HUB Mart donations. Coordinate with the Development Department to solicit monetary donations.
* Responsible for supplies inventory, management and ordering.
* Responsible for arranging meeting room requests.
* Provides transportation and/or coordinates client transportation HUB/ILP events.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor’s Degree plus 2 years of comparable work experience. Experience working with foster care system, probation and/or transition age clients, or personal experience in the above. Experience working with culturally diverse clients required. Knowledge of local Child Welfare and Juvenile Probation policies, procedures and governing legislation preferred, but not required.

**Required Skills/Abilities:**

* Driving is a requirement of the job. Must have possession of current driver’s license, access to a vehicle and personal automobile insurance. Carry a valid driver’s license, copy of vehicle registration, and Insurance in the event that coordinator needs to pick-up food donation, buying
* general food/supplies, and transporting clients.
* Current CPR and First Aid Certification required (or complete within 30 days of hire).
* Fingerprinting/background check as required by the Department of Justice and/or Title XXII regulations. TB test required.
* Must be punctual, efficient and organized; effective and professional under pressure. Ability to balance excellent client care with meeting deadlines and ensuring positive program goals and outcomes. Excellent communication skills - must be personable and informative when presenting
* Bill Wilson Center programs and services.
* Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence. Must be able to communicate effectively. Bilingual communication skills are a plus.
* Ability to work with basic mathematical concepts as required for reporting.
* Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.
* To perform this job successfully, an individual should have knowledge of Internet software; spreadsheet software and word processing software and Internet research skills.

**Physical Demands:**

* The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.
* Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to move and remain stationary, communicate, gather information and record information.
* The employee must occasionally move up to 20 pounds

jobs.description:
Salary Estimate: $145600.00 - $218400.00 / year  
Learn more about the benefits offered for this job.  

The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range of candidates hired. Factors that may be used to determine your actual salary may include your specific skills, how many years of experience you have and comparison to other employees already in this role. The typical candidate is hired below midpoint of the range.

As a Stroke Program Coordinator, your voice to influence patient care is valued and empowered at every turn –whether through open, collaborative relationships with your direct manager or more formal opportunities through hospital councils and national nursing initiatives. You'll help shape decisions that elevate both patient outcomes and the future of nursing.

##### **Job Summary and Qualifications**

* Under general supervision, and according to general policies and procedures, as the Stroke Program Coordinator you will develop and implement the Good Samaritan Hospital Stroke Program
* You will assess and analyze outcome measures for continued JCAHO Stroke Center certification, identify educational needs and provide comprehensive education pertaining to stroke intervention, prevention and rehabilitation for inpatients and community
* You will collaborate with nursing management and the Education Department to develop and implement staff education related to stroke issues and make regular rounds on stroke patients to evaluate appropriateness of treatment plan and nursing intervention

###### **What qualifications you will need:**

* Graduate of an accredited School of Nursing required
* Masters Degree Preferred
* Current California Registered Nurse license required
* Current California Board of Registered Nursing Practitioner preferred
* Basic Cardiac Life Support required
* ACLS required
* NIH Stroke Certification required
* 2 Years in acute medical/surgical/ neurological nursing preferred
* Computer literate with in-depth knowledge, experience to operate word processing, data bases, graphics, and spreadsheets in order to generate reports. Ability to learn and operate Krono’s, Meditech, Excel, Word and a patient care management systems. Ability to concentrate, with attention to detail in order to resolve patient care problems and identify patient needs. Ability to show understanding, patience, and tact when dealing with physicians, staff, and the public

* **Comprehensive benefits** for medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, behavioral health and telemedicine services

* **Savings and retirement resources**, including a 401(k) Plan with a 100% match on 3% to 9% of pay (based on years of service), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, flexible spending accounts, preferred banking partnerships, retirement readiness tools, rollover support and financial wellbeing counseling
* **Education support** through tuition assistance, student loan assistance, certification support, dependent scholarships and a partnership with Galen College of Nursing
* **Additional benefits** for fertility and family building, adoption assistance, life insurance, supplemental health protection plans, auto and home insurance, legal counseling, identity theft protection and consumer discounts

Learn more about Employee Benefits

Erica Rossitto, MBA/HCM, BSN, RN, NEA-BC

HCA Healthcare

Good Samaritan Hospital has been serving Silicon Valley since 1965, giving patient's access to highly-trained physicians and advanced technology. Our 470+ bed facility is a recognized leader in advanced cardiology services and provides a full array of diagnostic and interventional coronary peripheral services. jobs.title: Program Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Covenant House California (CHC) is a nonprofit organization that provides sanctuary and support for youth overcoming homelessness, ages 18-24. CHC believes that no young person deserves to be homeless; that every young person in California deserves housing, food, clothing, education, and most importantly, to be loved. CHC provides a full continuum of services to meet the physical, emotional, educational, vocational, and spiritual well-being of young people.

CHC’s doors are open to youth and staff regardless of their race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We believe that youth and team members deserve to be in an environment that is inclusive and affirming; where everyone is treated with dignity and respect and valued and appreciated for who they are. Maintaining a diverse community of youth and staff is key to our ability to achieve our mission most effectively. We are also committed to being a leader in advancing anti-racism, and to promoting opportunities for the free expression of the lived experiences of our youth and staff.

We are looking for people who, like us, believe that every young person deserves a place to belong. We think it takes all kinds of people to create diverse solutions to end youth homelessness and we are on a committed journey to build an inclusive and equitable work culture that brings out the best in everyone.

Covenant House California offers an excellent benefits package, (most benefits effective date of hire), including medical, vision, dental, an EAP program, 403b retirement account, and a generous vacation package.

**Position Summary**

The Program Project Coordinator provides high-level administrative and programmatic support directly to the Chief Program Officer (CPO), helping manage the CPO’s calendar, communications, and day-to-day priorities so the CPO can focus on leading the Program Division effectively. This role will also support the Norcal and Socal SVP’s with special projects, policy/procedures and any duties as assigned to help strengthen program operations and consistency across the state.

This role blends traditional administrative program responsibilities – calendar management, meeting logistics, audit preparations, meeting note compilation and travel coordination – with ownership of special program related project assignments given directly by the CPO. The right person is highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable anticipating CPO and SVP’s needs before being asked. They work behind the scenes to keep information flowing, fill various gaps needing administrative support, keep deadlines on track, and the CPO prepared for every meeting – including supporting the tracking of trainings, professional development logistics, and other administrative systems that keep the Program Division organized and unified.

The ideal candidate brings strong administrative and project coordination experience, sound judgment, a passion for serving young people experiencing homelessness and the discretion needed to support a busy executive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

**What Success Looks Like**

* In the first 90 days, the Program Project Coordinator will:
* Complete onboarding, including learning CHC’s program structure and meeting the Program Leadership team
* Take over calendar, scheduling, and meeting coordination for the CPO
* Establish organized tracking systems for the CPO and SVP’s special projects, trainings, and meeting follow-ups
* Build a clear working rhythm and communication style with the CPO

**By the end of year one, the Program Project Coordinator will have:**

* Become the CPO’s trusted, go-to resource for scheduling, logistics, and administrative coordination
* Successfully managed several special program related project assignments from start to finish
* Built reliable systems for tracking trainings, onboarding logistics, and program documentation
* Earned the CPO’s confidence as someone who keeps things organized and follows through

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Executive & Calendar Support**

* Manage the CPO’s scheduling, calendar coordination, travel planning, and related logistics, support SVP’s administrative needs as well.
* Coordinate logistics for meetings the CPO leads or attends, including agendas, preparation, action items and follow-ups
* Draft power point presentations, briefing documents, and talking points as directed by the CPO
* Organize and maintain the CPO’s SharePoint folders and internal filing systems

**Special Projects:**

* Own and run special project assignments that are program focused given directly by the CPO, from planning through completion
* Coordinate logistics for the CPO’s tours, speaking engagements, and site visits, including pre-event preparation and follow-up
* Track action items and deadlines on the CPO’s behalf to keep cross-department work moving forward
* Assist the CPO with grant and funder reporting by gathering information and compiling draft materials in collaboration with the Development team

**Training & Program Documentation Support:**

* Maintain tracking tools and attendance systems that support the professional development and training function, at the CPO’s direction and in partnership with the Senior Director of Program Training & Professional Development
* Support onboarding logistics for new program leaders, including scheduling, materials, and checklists
* Help maintain and distribute policy and procedure updates, including notes and follow-ups from relevant Covenant House International (CHI) calls(SCPO Calls, Presidium checklist, Quarterly Data review calls)
* Maintain internal tracking and reporting tools the CPO uses to keep the division organized

**Meeting & Communications Support:**

* Prepare meeting materials, one-pagers, and presentation decks as directed by the CPO
* Take notes and minutes at meetings the CPO attends and distribute follow-up items
* Serve as a point of contact for internal and external inquiri

jobs.title: Case Manager
jobs.description:
**CASE MANAGER I and II**

**Case Manager I - $2,621.57****-** **$3,873.25****Bi-weekly; $68,160.82****-** **$100,704.50****Annually**

**Case Manager II - $2,726.40****-** **$4,028.14****Bi-weekly; $70,886.40****-** **$104,731.64****Annually**

**New hires with no prior Regional Center work experience will start at the very beginning of the salary scale.**

**\* Please note that our new hire date is anticipated to be Monday, January 4th \***

The Regional Center of the East Bay (RCEB) is one of 21 Regional Centers that are community-based, private non-profit corporations under contract with the California Department of Developmental Services. RCEB provides intake, assessment, diagnosis, and coordinates community-based services for over 25,000 children and adults with developmental disabilities in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.

RCEB envisions a future where persons with developmental disabilities are truly a part of the community. Persons with developmental disabilities receive supports and services they need to succeed. The supports and services change as the need changes.

In our dream, children with developmental disabilities live with families in typical communities. Many choose to attend their neighborhood schools and play with neighborhood friends. Adults with developmental disabilities live in the residence of their choice – with family members, with friends, or with their spouse / significant other. They engage in activities of their choice – work, volunteering, education, training, or leisure. They have meaningful relationships with friends and coworkers and are seen as valuable, contributing members of their communities.

**Key Responsibilities**:

**Case Managers** are an integral part of realizing our dream. Under general direction, Case Managers are responsible for the entire case management process, including: assessment and evaluation, planning, authorizing, advocacy, monitoring, reviewing documentation for completion.

* Facilitate the planning process and develop the Individual Program Plan (IPP) or Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for assigned Consumers and oversee the implementation of the IPP/IFSP. Monitor and evaluate the services provided through the plan.

* Coordinate and support the implementation of the Consumers plan which may include identifying natural supports and generic services and evaluating when a need exists that can only be met through RCEB authorized funding.

* Advocate on behalf of consumers to protect their rights under the law and ensure that they receive those services and benefits to which they are entitled.

* Assist the consumer and family in obtaining essential diagnosis and evaluation from appropriate practitioners and secure written reports and other information which assesses and interprets the consumer's situation.

* Monitor the consumer's health and safety.

* Maintain all documentation and contacts as required by law, regulation and policy.

* Implement RCEB policies and procedures.

* Complete, in a timely manner, functional and/or developmental reviews.

* Keep supervisor informed of the status of the case load and unmet needs in the community.

* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualification:**

**Case Manager I**

* BA Degree in Social Work, Psychology or a related human services field and 1 year similar experience. OR B.A. in an unrelated human services field plus 4 years of experience working directly with the developmentally disabled.

* Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, verbally and in writing.

* Automobile and valid driver's license required.

* Demonstrate cultural awareness and sensitivity and an ability to work effectively with culturally diverse populations.

**Case Manager II**

* Master's Degree in Social Work, Psychology or related human services field.

* Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, verbally and in writing.

* Automobile and valid driver's license required.

* Demonstrate cultural awareness and sensitivity and an ability to work effectively with culturally diverse populations.

**Benefits:**

At the Regional Center of the Easy Bay, we offer a full spectrum of competitive benefits including:

* 3 weeks paid vacation + 12 sick days
* 14 paid holidays + 3 floating holidays
* Multiple options for medical care (including Kaiser at 100% employer paid for employee)
* Dental and vision plans
* CalPERs Retirement (pension),
* Student Loan Forgiveness\*
* Flex schedule, if applicable
* Work at Home schedules, if applicable
* Employee Assistance Program, including mental health care

* *The Public Service Loan Forgiveness program is a federal program that forgives student loan debt for nonprofit employees after 120 qualifying payments. Employees who work at least 30 hours per week for a governmental, 501(c)(3) nonprofit, or other qualifying nonprofit organization may apply to have the balance of their student loans forgiven (tax free) after making 120 monthly payments.*

*Regional Center of the East Bay (RCEB) does not discriminate against job applicants on account of race, color, creed or religion, national origin including language use restrictions, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition or HIV/AIDS status, political affiliation, military or veteran status, genetic characteristics, or ancestry.*

jobs.title: OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR
jobs.description:
Courier Company is seeking an experienced **Operations Supervisor** to lead a growing last-mile pickup and delivery operation based in **San Jose, CA**, serving customers throughout the Bay Area.

The Supervisor will assist in overseeing a team of drivers, working closely with management and customers while ensuring safe, efficient, and cost-effective operations. The position will focus on driver leadership, delivery KPIs, safety and security, route optimization, customer service, asset management, and basic payroll functions. Promotional opportunies for the right candidate who demonstrates initiative, work ethic, and pride in results!

Schedule

**Full-Time | Monday–Friday | 4:00 AM–1:00 PM**

**Key Responsibilities**

* Help lead and support a team of drivers.
* Monitor delivery performance and ensure customer KPIs are met.
* Train and coach drivers on safety, service, and operational initiatives.
* Support route optimization and productivity improvement projects.
* Perform basic payroll and timekeeping functions.
* Conduct hub audits and enforce safety and security procedures.
* Resolve escalated delivery issues and communicate with customers.
* Identify operational challenges and implement effective solutions.

* Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

**Benefits**

* Health Insurance

* Monday–Friday Schedule
* Opportunity for Advancement

Pay: $75,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year

* Health insurance

jobs.title: Operations Supervisor - NF
jobs.description:
Sims Metal (Sims) is a global leader in metal recycling. With facilities across the globe, Sims plays an intrinsic role in the circular economy by making resources available for future use. As a responsible corporate citizen, we continuously seek new ways to broaden our participation in the environmental sector, ensuring that our future is as bright, safe, and secure as at any time in our long history.

Job Summary:

This position is responsible for overseeing the processing of scrap as efficiently as possible while promoting an accident-free and environmentally compliant workplace. The Yard Supervisor is also responsible for oversight of the yard personnel and day to day operations including maintenance on equipment, monthly inspections, and safety.

Essential Responsibilities:

* Works with site and regional staff, vendor/suppliers, and clients/customers.
* Operations necessary equipment to process material.
* Oversees yard operations including guiding employees.
* May order and purchases parts and equipment.
* May perform weekly and monthly inspections of all equipment and machinery.
* Schedules preventive maintenance on equipment.
* Maintains site and equipment maintenance records.
* Responsible for troubleshooting hydraulic problems and directing personnel in repairing equipment.
* Responsible for enforcement of safety regulations.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

Sills and Experience:

* Must have 3 – 5 years applicable industry experience or related industry.
* Minimum of 2 years supervisory experience preferred.
* Undergraduate degree or equivalent work experience.
* Must be willing to work in shop area and outdoor environment in all types of weather.
* Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Fluency in Spanish a plus.
* Strong analytical and mathematical skills.
* Must have excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to find suitable solutions for productivity, environmental, safety-related, and employment issues.
* Minimum of 2 years’ experience in mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical repairs on heavy equipment and machinery desired.
* Commercial license (Class A) a plus.
* Must have some knowledge of computers.
* Working knowledge of tools and equipment used in a scrap yard including but not limited to: torches, cranes, loaders, forklifts, bobcats, shears, balers, and other production-related equipment.

A career with Sims provides you with the opportunity to work with an organization whose goal is to be the world’s safest and most responsible recycling company. Our people achieve this by creating a zero-harm workplace, being exemplary members of the communities in which we operate, and being responsible stewards of the environment. We also offer competitive pay and a range of attractive benefits.

Sims is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value the diversity of all of our employees and are committed to creating an inclusive working environment where everyone can contribute, advance on merit, and realize their full potential. Sims does not discriminate with regard to race, sex, religion, color, national origin, citizenship status, disability, age, marital or familial status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, housing status, source of income, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local laws. This applies to any employment decision, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. qualified applicants with a disability in need of a reasonable accommodation may request such without fear of reprisal or discrimination.

To achieve our purpose to create a world without waste to preserve our planet, we are guided by our Principles of Purpose: Be Safe + Well, Band Together, Be Accountable + Transparent, Consistently Innovate, Inspire with Purpose, Celebrate + Have Fun.

jobs.title: Regional Operations Manager - Dermatology
jobs.description:
**About Metropolis Dermatology**

We do derm differently. Our mission is to make healthy skin accessible to everyone by providing the highest quality medical and cosmetic dermatology care. Metropolis Dermatology is growing rapidly, with plans to expand our footprint throughout California. We're looking for passionate, self-motivated do-ers to help us execute on our bold mission.

**About the Role**

As a Regional Operations Manager, you are accountable for the performance of a group of Metropolis clinics: operational excellence, financial results, patient satisfaction, and growth. You lead and develop the Practice Supervisors who run each clinic day to day. You partner with each site's Clinical Director and executive leadership to turn Metropolis strategy into results on the ground. You are a builder. You raise the standard across your region, spot problems early, and help the company scale to new locations.

**Home base and region:** This role is based in San Jose. You will oversee a group of Metropolis clinics assigned by leadership, with regular travel between them. Our clinics are in Downtown LA, Brentwood, Pasadena, Costa Mesa, and San Jose. Mileage between clinics is reimbursed.

**What You'll Do**

*Regional Operations Leadership*

* Own operational performance across all clinics in your region and hold each clinic to Metropolis standards
* Partner with each Clinical Director to align workflows with clinical requirements and build and execute clinic business plans
* Visit clinics regularly to observe operations, coach supervisors, and solve problems in person
* Standardize best practices and share what works across clinics
* Lead change management for new systems, policies, and initiatives
* Lead complex operational and patient service escalations

*Financial Performance & Growth*

* Manage clinic financial outcomes, including budgets, labor and staffing models, supply spend, and productivity
* Review clinic KPIs (visit volume, schedule utilization, access and wait times, revenue, and cost) and drive action plans
* Identify growth opportunities, including patient access, retention, and service mix
* Support new clinic launches, including staffing, training, and readiness
* Conduct monthly productivity dashboard reviews with clinicians in partnership with Clinical Directors

*Patient & Provider Satisfaction*

* Lead regional patient experience improvement, including feedback, trends, and complaints
* Develop and implement consistent service standards, and ensure supervisors reinforce them daily
* Build strong working relationships with providers and clinical leadership
* Close the loop on issues and recommend system or process fixes

*People Leadership*

* Lead hiring and onboarding of Practice Supervisors. Set clear expectations, coach, and conduct performance reviews
* Develop supervisors into strong leaders and build a bench for future growth
* Partner with HR on recruiting, retention, and succession for clinic staff roles
* Hold regular 1:1s and team meetings, and give timely, candid feedback

*Compliance & Risk*

* Ensure regional compliance with HIPAA, OSHA, and healthcare and employment regulations
* Conduct periodic clinic audits and track corrective actions
* Lead regional rollout of digital tools and AI-driven technologies, such as AI scribes, with proper security, compliance, and change management

**Must Have**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience
* 5+ years of operations experience in multi-site healthcare, ambulatory, or similar service environments
* 2+ years managing managers or supervisors
* Experience owning budgets, staffing models, or a clinic or multi-site P&L
* Strong analytical skills and comfort using KPIs to drive decisions
* Proven track record leading change management and healthcare technology rollouts, including AI-driven solutions
* Strong grasp of HIPAA, data privacy, and security considerations for new technology in healthcare operations
* Exceptional leadership, coaching, and communication skills

jobs.title: Strategy and Operations Manager, AI-Native Business Operations
jobs.description:
**Own Every Moment at NetApp**

At NetApp, your ideas power innovation. We lead in intelligent data infrastructure—delivering unified storage, integrated data services, and solutions that help organizations unlock the full potential of their data, from AI to multicloud.

Ready to innovate and contribute to our path to $10B? Here, you'll collaborate with passionate teams, tackle real-world challenges, and see your impact in how customers transform and grow. If you're ready to bring curiosity, creativity, and drive to every moment, NetApp is where your journey begins. Join teams that innovate to elevate, drive results, and excel together across every function.

**Strategy and Operations Manager, AI-Native Business Operations**
==================================================================

San Jose, California, United States

**Job category:** Business Operations **Job ID:** 137017-en\_US

**Job Summary**
---------------

This role helps the leaders of NetApp's product organization decide where people and money go, and makes those decisions faster and better informed. It spans planning, forecasting and tracking the organization's people and resources, and the budget across headcount, open reqs, software, cloud and AI spend. On each of these the analyst brings a point of view, not just the numbers behind it.

The role combines three skillsets that usually live in three different people: the consultant who frames an ambiguous question and lands a recommendation with senior leaders; the analyst who builds the model and can defend every number in it; and the AI-first builder who turns recurring work into systems that run themselves. The unit of delivery is a better decision, made sooner, on numbers leaders trust.

The role sits within the AI-Native Business Operations team in the product organization, and reports to the Director, AI-Native Business Operations. The team works in close partnership with Finance, HR, Talent Acquisition and engineering leadership across the product organization.

A few principles shape how the team approaches its work:

* **We start from outcomes, not from tasks.** The first question on any piece of work is what it is for and what good looks like, not how to automate the current steps.
* **One source of truth.** People, plans and spend live in one trusted, connected source, and every report and dashboard draws from it.
* **AI first, with human judgment throughout.** AI shortens the time to an outcome; our judgment tests every assumption and validates each step, from the source data to the final recommendation.
* **Accountability does not stop at the answer.** The analyst stands behind the method and the data as well as the result.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* **Plan, forecast and track.** Build the plans and forecasts for the product organization's people and resources, and track them month by month: where engineering capacity and spend go across products and investment themes, and how hiring, attrition and backfills move against plan.
* **Manage the budget.** Hold the product organization's spend against target with Finance, from headcount and open reqs to software, cloud and AI, and find where to consolidate, renegotiate or stop.
* **Advise product leadership.** Turn the numbers into a clear point of view for vice presidents and their staff, and run the planning cycles and leadership reviews where those decisions get made.
* **Operationalize strategic initiatives.** Take a leadership priority from idea to working program: define its scope, set milestones and checkpoints, build the plan and put it in motion, then measure the results and keep leadership updated as it lands.
* **Automate the recurring work.** Build agents, automations and dashboards with Claude and the team's other AI tools that make each cycle take less effort than the last.
* **Keep the source of truth trustworthy.** Maintain the connected data behind every leadership view, with the checks and audit trail that let a leader defend any figure in front of Finance or the executive staff.
* **Work across functions.** Partner with Finance, HR, Talent Acquisition, IT and data owners on access, definitions and changes, within NetApp standards for privacy and acceptable use.

**Education and Experience**
----------------------------

* Typically requires a minimum of 8 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience, including a minimum of 3 years in consulting. This experience may have been gained in:

* The strategy, operations or analytics practice of a management consulting firm, such as McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Deloitte, or a comparable practice
* A business operations, strategy and operations, or FP&A team at an AI-first technology company
* A founding or early operating role at a startup building AI-native products

* Uses AI as the default way of working, across analysis, writing and building, with examples to show, and builds validation into each step so the speed never costs accuracy. Familiarity with Claude Code or Cursor is preferred.
* Learns new domains, systems and data quickly, and acts without waiting for a perfect brief; comfortable where the problem is still being defined.
* Expert scenario and financial modeling: headcount, cost and what-if models that leaders use to make decisions, and the judgment to spot when a number is wrong.
* A technical, hands-on approach to data: reads data architectures and table schemas, writes the joins in SQL or Python, and treats data preparation as part of the job, from cleaning and de-duplicating records to validating formats and keys before any number is used. Experience with workforce or finance data in systems such as Workday or Snowflake is a plus.
* A track record of influencing directors and vice presidents without authority, with recommendations that were acted on.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to disagree productively and adjust as evidence evolve

We’re not your average law firm. We specialize in serving healthcare professionals with a high standard of excellence—and we know how to have fun doing it. You’ll work with great people, meaningful clients, and enjoy room to grow professionally.

**About Earned**  
Earned is a category-defining, first-in-kind tax-smart financial services firm dedicated to serving doctors, their families, and their practices. Our goal is to be the only financial partner doctors need by seamlessly integrating personal and practice-based solutions to maximize their wealth potential and drive better financial outcomes.

We bring together tax, accounting, wealth management, insurance, and legal services under one platform not as a generic one-stop shop, but to deliver better advice through an integrated view of a doctor’s full financial life. Our differentiation is relationship-led, trust-based selling paired with disciplined execution across the ecosystem.

Earned manages $3.4B+ in assets, serves more than 20,000 clients, and is one of the fastest-growing doctor-focused platforms in the country. Backed by $200M of committed capital, we are scaling rapidly through acquisitions and organic growth across multiple service lines.

We are building this platform from the ground up, leveraging modern technology, data, and AI to simplify the client experience and make it easier for advisors and sales teams to deliver high-quality advice at scale. Operating across multiple service lines, acquired entities and client entry points require a highly disciplined, yet relationship-driven go-to-market model that can scale without losing trust.

Join us as we build the future of financial services for doctors faster, smarter, and at scale.

**Job Summary**The Operations Manager oversees the firm’s day-to-day operations, combining office management, client intake and matter assignment, and firm-wide operations in one role. In this position, you will keep the office running smoothly, route new matters to the right attorney, and lead the non-attorney team, all in direct support of the firm’s goal annual revenue goal.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Reporting Structure & Team***

* **Direct reports:** All non-attorney support and administrative staff, including the receptionist, biller, and marketing assistant. Partners with the marketing lead (shared with Earned corporate) on firm-specific priorities.
* **Collaborates** **with, but** **does not directly supervise:** The firm’s attorneys (four full-time transactional attorneys, two full-time litigators, one part-time litigator, and an incoming full-time litigator) and two paralegals, who continue to report to their supervising attorneys on case work. Coordinates with attorneys on caseload capacity and with paralegals on scheduling; legal supervision of matters remains with the attorneys.
* **Escalation:** Escalates any staffing, client, or vendor issue that cannot be resolved independently directly to the Managing Attorney.

***Office & Administrative Management***

* Oversee the physical office, including facilities, security, supplies, and vendor relationships (IT, copiers, cleaning, insurance, and utilities
* Negotiate and administer vendor and service contracts, owning renewal dates and ongoing cost review
* Manage firm calendars and conference room scheduling, and coordinate attorney travel and CLE/seminar logistics
* Oversee front-desk and telephone operations performed by the receptionist, ensuring consistently professional client-facing standards
* Manage office supply budgets and approve related purchases
* Maintain personnel files, PTO records, and documented office policies and procedures
* Serve as the primary liaison to building management and the point of contact for office-related emergencies

***Operations, Process & Systems***

* Own, document, and continuously improve the firm’s operational workflows, including matter intake, conflict checks, engagement letters, document management, and practice management software, redesigning processes to use automation and AI where it improves speed, accuracy, or client experience
* Monitor compliance and filing deadlines across transactional and litigation matters to ensure no deadline is missed
* Partner with the biller to ensure invoicing is accurate and timely, and monitor collections against the firm’s average billable rate
* Administer and enforce the firm’s flat-fee schedule, and route non-standard matters to appropriate person for fee quotes
* Develop and maintain operational dashboards and reporting that measure firm performance against the annual revenue goal
* Identify process bottlenecks and recommend technology or staffing solutions to Managing Attorney
* Track firm-wide profitability, attorney production, and collections, and report notable trends to Managing Attorney
* Lead the firm’s AI and automation initiatives: identify high-value use cases across intake, scheduling, billing, collections, document drafting and review, knowledge management, and client communication; evaluate and pilot tools; manage rollout; and measure results (time saved, error reduction, cost impact)
* Develop and maintain the firm’s AI use policy, in coordination with the Managing Attorney and attorneys, covering approved tools, client confidentiality and data security, vendor due diligence, and required attorney review of any AI-assisted legal work product
* Train attorneys and staff on approved AI tools and workflows, and keep written procedures and prompt libraries up to dat

Description:

Beveridge & Diamond, P.C., the foremost national corporate environmental law firm, is seeking an eDiscovery Project Manager to lead the planning and execution of complex electronic discovery matters across the litigation lifecycle.

Working under the general direction of the Director of Litigation Support & eDiscovery, the Project Manager serves as the primary operational lead for assigned matters and partners with attorneys, litigation support professionals, review teams, clients, and external service providers to deliver efficient, accurate, and defensible discovery solutions. The role applies advanced eDiscovery expertise and independent judgment to manage competing priorities, identify and mitigate project risks, recommend technical approaches, and maintain accountability for project outcomes.

The Project Manager operates with significant autonomy in the execution of assigned matters while escalating substantive legal decisions and significant strategic, financial, staffing, technology-investment, or departmental matters to the Director or responsible case team.

At Beveridge & Diamond, we do not just practice environmental law—we define it. With more than 170 lawyers across seven U.S. offices and a legacy spanning five decades, we are The Environmental Law Firm. **Project Management and Execution**

* Develop, implement, and maintain project plans for assigned eDiscovery matters, including scope, schedules, milestones, resource requirements, dependencies, quality requirements, and deliverables.

* Translate attorney-approved discovery requirements into processing and production specifications and work with technical personnel and vendors to confirm data completeness, metadata accuracy, document relationships, and resolution of processing exceptions.
* Evaluate and recommend appropriate use of eDiscovery tools, search methods, early case assessment, analytics, technology-assisted review, and related technologies.
* Support implementation and validation of AI-enabled discovery workflows, including data preparation, issue-prompt refinement, workflow configuration, pilot testing, sampling, quality control, and documentation, in coordination with the Director and case team.

**Budget and Resource Management**

* Prepare project cost estimates and budgets based on anticipated scope, data volumes, staffing, hosting, and vendor requirements.

**Quality Assurance and Risk Management**

* Establish and oversee project-level quality assurance procedures for data processing, review workflows, and productions.
* Perform or coordinate production quality control, including checks of production scope, redactions, privilege exclusions, metadata, load files, and output specifications; resolve discrepancies and obtain required approvals before release.
* Monitor technical deliverables for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and compliance with established requirements.
* Identify operational, technical, scheduling, and resource risks and implement appropriate mitigation measures within established authority.
* Escalate significant issues affecting discovery obligations, project scope, costs, or case strategy to appropriate stakeholders and maintain documentation supporting defensible discovery practices.

**Attorney and Stakeholder Coordination**

* Serve as the primary operational point of contact for assigned eDiscovery projects and lead appropriate kickoff and status meetings.

* Translate technical information into practical recommendations that support informed case-team decisions.
* Facilitate communication and accountability among internal personnel, external vendors, and other project stakeholders.

jobs.description:
### **Position Summary:**

This position manages SFRRN grants and contracts and supports operations across its 8 network partners, while collaborating with community organizations, coalitions, and government agencies. The SFRRN Program Manager also partners closely with the SFILEN Program Manager and supervises the SFILEN & SFRRN Program Coordinator.

### 

### **About Chinese for Affirmative Action (CAA)**

CAA was founded in 1969 to protect the civil and political rights of Chinese Americans and to advance multiracial democracy in the United States. Today, CAA is a progressive voice in and on behalf of the broader Asian American and Pacific Islander community. CAA advocates for systemic change that protects immigrant rights, promotes language diversity, and remedies racial and social injustice.

### 

### **About SF Rapid Response Network (SFRRN)**

The San Francisco Rapid Response Network (SFRRN) is a 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, immigration enforcement response hotline serving the City of San Francisco. Founded in 2008, and revamped in 2016, SFRRN was one of the first, and remains one of the few 24/7 immigration enforcement response hotlines in the country. SFRRN houses 8 immigration focused community based organizations who staff the 24/7 hotline, verifies immigration enforcement activity in San Francisco, connects San Franciscans to legal and accompaniment services, and provides immigration centered Know-Your-Rights education to immigrant community members citywide.

  

In 2026, CAA became the lead and fiscal agency to house the San Francisco Immigrant Legal & Education Network (SFILEN) and SFRRN. As a founding and active member of these networks, CAA is committed to the health and wellbeing of both collaboratives in order that partners may continue to serve immigrant communities with immigration legal services and community education in the face of heightened immigration enforcement and rising xenophobia.

### 

### **Position Description**

Reporting to the Managing Director of Programs, the Program Manager manages SFRRN grants and contracts, oversees and supports network operations amongst the 8 partners, and works closely with other community based organizations, collaboratives, and government entities to ensure the success of these strategies. Some partner groups include: The San Francisco Immigrant Legal Defense Collaborative, California Coalition for Immigrant Justice, Northern California Rapid Response Networks, Bay Area Rapid Response Networks, as well as entities coordinating accompaniment, verification, and city agencies such as the Mayor’s Office, Office of Civic Engagement and Immigrant Affairs, San Francisco Police Department and San Francisco Sheriff's Office. As an Associate Program Manager, CX, you'll shape how millions of customers experience Kikoff end to end, turning customer insight into the systems and improvements that make every interaction better. You'll pinpoint the highest-impact gaps, decide where AI automation, CX tooling, and measurement will move the needle for customers and the business, and take solutions from idea to completion in order to drive measurable impact.

When part of the product is causing friction, you’ll bring the data, work with Product and Engineering to fix the root cause, and help define how we measure CX, including contact rate, CSAT, and customer risk signals.

* Build our AI chatbot strategy (coverage, containment, resolution quality)

  + Agent-assist / "copilot" workflows to reduce manual effort and errors

**CX Tooling**

* Improve and maintain core CX systems (e.g., Zendesk, workflows, CSAT collection)
* Support development of internal tools that increase agent and team efficiency
* Help standardize tooling and workflows across support channels

**Measurement & Insights**

* Analyze CX performance across channels (chatbot, support, product journeys)
* Identify friction points not captured in support tickets (e.g., drop-offs, dead ends), and work with the Product team to resolve them
* Build and maintain dashboards to track key CX metrics and initiative impact

**Cross-functional execution**

* Partner with Customer Operations, Product, and Data teams to implement solutions
Own initiatives end-to-end: problem definition solution design launch* measurement
* Translate customer insights and data into actionable improvements

* Hands-on experience with CX tools (Zendesk, chat platforms, CSAT tools)
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Ability to operate in ambiguous environments and drive execution
* Experience working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, or Operations teams
* High ownership and bias toward action

* Exposure to automation, workflows, or AI-driven tools

jobs.title: Facilities Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
**SALARY RANGE**

$82,000 to $87,000 Annually

**GENERAL DESCRIPTION**

The Facilities Project Coordinator supports the day-to-day operations of the Building Operations department through coordination of facilities requests, work orders, vendor activities, preventive maintenance workflows, and operational administration. The position serves as a central point of coordination and follow-through, helping ensure facilities activities are organized, tracked, communicated, and completed in a timely and consistent manner.

Working under the supervision of the Senior Project Manager, the Facilities Project Coordinator operates with initiative and appropriate autonomy to manage routine workflows, resolve issues within established procedures, and escalate matters requiring technical, budgetary, compliance, or leadership decisions.

This position supports strategic facility initiatives of the organization anticipated to occur over a two-year period. It is anticipated that employment in this position will continue through approximately fall 2028. The Facilities Project Coordinator role is an at-will position; length of employment will be determined based on project completion dates and schedules.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Work Order & Issue Management**

* Support the coordination of facilities requests alongside Facilities Operations team, ensuring each issue is logged, prioritized, assigned, communicated, and closed with documented follow-through.
* Administer the Angus work order system, including ticket review, assignment coordination, status tracking, reporting, user support, and workflow maintenance.
* Monitor open, overdue, recurring, and unresolved service requests; follow up proactively and escalate safety concerns, delays, or items requiring technical, budgetary, compliance, or leadership decisions.
* Assist the Facilities Operations Manager with scheduling vendors for planned maintenance, urgent service needs, and unplanned repairs.
* Coordinate work orders, vendor activity, preventive maintenance, and corrective actions through completion, confirming that required documentation and closeout information are recorded.
* Communicate service impacts, access needs, project updates, and work status to staff, vendors, and other stakeholders.

**Facility Inspections & Follow-Through**

* Coordinate quarterly facility walkthroughs with preschool site directors, document identified needs, submit work orders, and track completion.
* Coordinate quarterly inspections across all sites with Facilities and Program Support teams, document findings, open and assign work orders, and follow through on corrective actions.

**Tracking, Documentation & Administration**

* Maintain facilities project and request trackers by logging new requests, updating priorities and status, and monitoring work from initiation through completion.
* Maintain organized shared drives so project documentation, communications, vendor records, and closeout materials are current and easy to retrieve.
* Manage routine facilities administration, including vendor records, invoice routing, purchasing support, reporting, and recordkeeping.

**Project & Operational Support**

* Assist with facilities and IT project coordination tasks, including scheduling, documentation, access coordination, status tracking, and follow-up for project managers.
* Coordinate contractor access and support operational readiness activities related to scheduled facilities work.
* Provide coverage for the Facilities Operations Manager during absences to maintain continuity of routine facilities workflows and issue escalation.
* Support facilities, compliance, process-improvement, and special projects as assigned, including documentation and workflow updates.

**REQUIREMENTS**

* Associate or bachelor’s degree, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Two or more years of experience in facilities coordination, workplace operations, office administration, property management, hospitality, or a similar operational support role.
* Experience coordinating maintenance requests, vendors, contractors, or service providers in a complex or high-volume environment.
* Experience using ticketing, work order, or maintenance management systems; Angus experience preferred.
* Highly meticulous with strong file management and record-keeping habits that hold up under a high volume of concurrent work.
* Demonstrated ability to work independently, take initiative, prioritize competing demands, and follow work through completion with limited supervision.
* Ability to process information and communicate clearly and concisely.
* Strong organizational, administrative, communication, and customer Service skills.
* Experience supporting purchasing, invoicing, vendor administration, or operational recordkeeping.
* Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, particularly Teams, SharePoint, and Lists.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**  
This position is primarily performed on-site at JCCSF facilities and includes work in office, program, storage, mechanical, and other operational spaces. Occasional remote work may be considered when appropriate for specific tasks and operational requirements.

The position requires regular movement throughout the facility and frequent interaction with staff, vendors, contractors, and members of the Building Operations team. The employee may occasionally encounter noise, dust, active maintenance work, mechanical equipment, and areas with varying temperatures.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**  
Duties include regular walking throughout the facility, standing, sitting, using stairs, accessing storage and operational areas, and performing physical tasks consistent with a facilities coordination position.

The employee must be able to lift and carry items weighing up to twenty pounds. Reasonable accommodation may be provided as appropriate.

**STATUS:** Benefited, non-exempt

**HOURS:** 40 hours per week

**SCHEDULE:** Monday - Friday, general business

jobs.title: Hospital Based Patient Advocate
jobs.description:
Make a real difference in patients’ lives—join **Elevate Patient Financial Solutions** as a **Hospital Based Patient Advocate** and help guide individuals through their healthcare financial journey. This full-time position is located 100**% onsite at a hospital in San Francisco, CA,**with a **Monday-Friday schedule from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM**. Driving required must have a valid drivers license.  
  
Bring your passion for helping others and grow with a company that values your impact. In 2024, our Advocates helped over 823,000 patients secure the Medicaid coverage they needed. Elevate’s mission is to make a difference. Are you ready to be the difference?  
  
As a **Hospital Based Patient Advocate**, you play a vital role in guiding uninsured hospital patients through the complex landscape of medical and disability assistance. This **onsite, hospital-based role** places you at the heart of patient financial advocacy—meeting individuals face-to-face, right in their hospital rooms, to guide them through the process of identifying eligibility and applying for financial assistance. Your presence and empathy make a real difference during some of life’s most vulnerable moments.  
  
**Job Summary**  
  
The purpose of this position is to connect uninsured hospital patients to programs that will cover their medical expenses. As a Patient Advocate, you will play a critical role in assisting uninsured hospital patients by evaluating their eligibility for various federal, state, and county medical or disability assistance programs through bed-side visits and in-person interactions. Your primary objective will be to guide patients face-to-face through the application process, ensuring thorough completion and follow-up. This role is crucial in ensuring that uninsured patients are promptly identified and assisted, with the goal of meeting our benchmark that 98% of patients are screened at bedside.  
  
**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Screen uninsured hospital patients at bedside in an effort to determine if patient is a viable candidate for federal, state, and/or county medical or disability assistance.
* Complete the appropriate applications and following through until approved.
* Detailed, accurate and timely documentation in both Elevate PFS and hospital systems on all cases worked.
* Provide exceptional customer service skills at all times.
* Maintain assigned work queue of patient accounts.
* Collaborate in person and through verbal/written correspondence with hospital staff, case managers, social workers, financial counselors.
* Answer incoming telephone calls, make out-bound calls, and track all paperwork necessary to submit enrollment and renewal for prospective Medicaid patients.
* Maintain structured and timely contact with the applicant and responsible government agency, by phone whenever possible or as structured via the daily work queue.
* Assist the applicant with gathering any additional reports or records, meeting appointment dates and times and arrange transportation if warranted.
* Conduct in-person community visits as needed to acquire documentation.
* As per established protocols, inform the client in a timely manner of all approvals and denials of coverage.
* Attend ongoing required training to remain informed about current rules and regulations related to governmental programs, and apply updated knowledge when working with patients and cases.
* Regular and timely attendance.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications and Requirements**  
  
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities.

* Some college coursework preferred
* Prior hospital experience preferred
* Adaptability when dealing with constantly changing processes, computer systems and government programs
* Professional experience working with state and federal programs
* Critical thinking skills
* Ability to maneuver throughout the hospital and patients’ rooms throughout scheduled work shift.
* Proficient experience utilizing Microsoft Office Suite with emphasis on Excel and Outlook
* Effectively communicate both orally and written, to a variety of individuals
* Ability to multitask to meet performance metrics while functioning in a fast-paced environment.
* Hospital-Based Patient Advocates are expected to dress in accordance with their respective Client’s Dress Code.
* Hybrid positions require home internet connections that meet the Company’s upload and download speed criteria. Hybrid employees working from home are expected to comply with Elevate’s Remote Work Policy, including but not limited to working in a private and dedicated workspace where confidential information can be shared in accordance with HIPAA and PHI requirements.

**Benefits**  
ElevatePFS believes in making a positive impact not only within our industry but also with our employees –the organization’s greatest asset! We take pride in offering comprehensive benefits in a vast array of plans that contribute to the present and future well-being of our employees and their families.

* Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
* 401K (100% match for the first 3% & 50% match for the next 2%)
* 15 days of PTO

* 2 Floating holidays
* 1 Elevate Day (floating holiday)
* Pet Insurance
* Employee referral bonus program
* Teamwork: We believe in teamwork and having fun together
* Career Growth: Gain great experience to promote to higher roles

jobs.description:
Trust & Safety - San Francisco

**About the team**

Trusted Access helps eligible customers access and use advanced AI capabilities with appropriate safeguards. Within User Safety & Risk Operations, we connect customer onboarding, eligibility review, access provisioning, and support into a service customers can navigate with confidence.

We work with Product, Engineering, technical support, regional operations, and customer-facing teams to resolve difficult access problems and improve the systems behind them. Our work combines sound judgment on individual cases with better products, clearer guidance, and automation that reduces unnecessary friction.

**About the role**

We’re looking for a senior operations leader to own the Trusted Access operating strategy and lead a team of risk-operations specialists. You will set priorities across programs, build a reliable customer access service, and hire, manage, and develop your direct reports.

This role combines program ownership with formal people management. You will establish shared commitments with technical support and regional escalation leaders, who manage their own teams, and bring those groups together around customer outcomes. You’ll stay close enough to complex cases to challenge assumptions while giving specialists the ownership and capacity to fix recurring problems.

Success means customers reach the right access outcome with clear communication, teams make consistent decisions, and the service scales with less avoidable escalation and manual work.

**In this role, you will:**

* Own the operating strategy and roadmap across Trusted Access programs, translating customer needs and organizational priorities into clear service commitments, ownership, and investment decisions.
* Build a coherent customer journey from application and eligibility review through approval, provisioning coordination, and confirmed access, including appeals and subsequent access changes. Establish clear handoffs and route exceptions to authorized decision-makers.
* Hireance gaps, and build the capabilities needed as programs grow.
* Make capacity and prioritization decisions across urgent customer needs, launch readiness, and lasting improvements. Coordinate regional coverage, vendor support, and backup with partner teams while protecting time to eliminate recurring work.
* Lead consequential customer escalations, bringing incomplete or conflicting evidence into a clear decision process. Align owners on the next action and ensure customers receive accurate updates and a clear resolution.
* Turn support patterns into a prioritized roadmap with Product and Engineering: improve onboarding, provisioning workflows, tooling, self-service, and AI-assisted operations. Validate that changes work before expanding them.
* Establish measures of service health and decision quality. Distinguish fast responses from actual resolution, investigate persistent delays, and use evidence to change priorities.
* Prepare new programs and customer channels for launch and scale. Align support responsibilities, review standards, customer guidance, and technical dependencies; make readiness gaps and tradeoffs clear to leadership.

**You might thrive in this role if you:**

* Have built and run complex customer support, onboarding, access, risk, or service operations, with measurable improvements beyond handling more volume.
* Have formally managed people through hiringance decisions, and can show how your leadership increased the team’s capability and ownership. 5+ years of management experience preferred.
* Can make defensible tradeoffs among customer commitments, safeguards, service quality, and capacity, even when stakeholders disagree or the evidence is incomplete.
* Have led work across teams you do not manage, resolving ownership gaps and negotiating commitments that hold up in execution.
* Are analytically and technically fluent enough to diagnose workflow failures, evaluate automation, and partner effectively on product and provisioning changes.
* Communicate with precision and empathy, from explaining an access blocker to a customer to presenting a difficult investment decision to leadership.
